description:
Participación individual del reto "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer"

Soy estudiante de Ingeniería en Telecomunicaciones y Redes, con mucho interés en la exploración espacial. Espero ser de gran ayuda en este proyecto y crear una experiencia distinta para futuras generaciones que tengan la curiosidad por aventurarse a el espacio.
summary:
Luna Base: Road to Mars is a browser-based management game where kids ages 7-12 run a lunar outpost with four astronauts. Each turn, players assign their crew to stations  to keep three resources alive: energy, life support, and shielding. If any bar reaches zero, the mission fails.

Players earn science points to upgrade each station and, once the base is strong, build a spacecraft to Mars. 

Losing is part of learning: each failure shows a short explanation of the real constraint behind it. The game teaches that deep space survival depends on balancing limited resources, a trade-off real mission planners face every day.
details:
Benefits and intended impact
Players experience a real constraint of deep space survival: limited power and limited crew must be split between staying alive and doing science. We want kids to understand that mission planners make these trade-offs daily, and that failure is a chance to learn. Each loss shows a short explanation of the constraint behind it.

Tools
I used Godot Engine for the development.

Creativity
Instead of an abstract quiz or poster, the game turns survival constraints into mechanics. We chose a pixel-art, retro-terminal style to make a technical topic approachable and fun.

Factors I consider
I kept the design to three resources so young players aren’t overwhelmed. I used whole numbers on 0–10 bars so that a child can read them at a glance. I also simulated thousands of games to tune the costs, so that a careful player reaches Mars around day 25, while an inattentive one fails early. We also avoided any “safe” option without a cost.
